3) So biological muscles for robotics seem like a great idea. But, I think that there could be a possibility that they may become obsolete in the future. 

This is, because there are already special materials that can mimic the properties of biological muscles. These materials are called artificial muscles. 

Artificial muscles can already do some things better than their organic counterparts. For example some types of artificial muscles can lift loads that are a dozen times, a hundred times, or even a thousand times heavier than what biological muscles can lift (however, from what I have been able to see, artificial muscles typically have terrible energy efficiencies, when they have higher lifting capabilities). In addition to this, some types of artificial muscles have better energy efficiencies than their biological counterparts (for example organic muscles typically have an energy efficiency of around 20-30%. In contrast some types of artificial muscles have energy efficiencies of around 80-90%). 

There are other properties (other than lifting capability, and energy efficiency) that judge the qualities of artificial muscles. But these 2 things are the ones that readily come to my mind.

While the area surrounding the crash site doesn’t seem as damaged as it should be, the surface is only a small part of this game. A lot of this game, if not most, takes place *below* the ocean floor in underwater caves. As for the batteries, most of the batteries found in this game are still sealed in Alterra containers when found. And even if the negative effects of the Aurora’s crash exceeded the map we are given to explore during the game, the game takes place on a thermal crater risen above the ocean floor. Overall you've made some very compelling arguments, but I feel I have to point out two potential oversights. Most glaring is that in the audio and text logs you can find scattered around the game, it is revealed that the captain of the ship stayed on board until the very end to make a controlled decent. While not a proper landing, I feel it lends some credence as to why the crash zone is as small as it is. Perhaps it wasn't a proper or gentle landing, but neither was it a full force crash from orbital height. Coupled with a few other theories I've seen, the site of the crash may not have actually been shallow water. There may have been some small degree of dry land, which would explain why the terrain goes so far up to meet the ship nearly all the way around, even poking above the water for a sizable area around the shull of the Aurora. 
Secondly, with the exception of the truly absurd number of water bottles required to survive, you don't encounter much actual plastic. There may even be reason to suggest the water bottles might not even be plastic as we understand it today. In some cases, they almost resemble more of a metallic container. Though I feel a lot was overlooked in the creation of the game on that point, as no materials are actually required to create the container the water goes into. The bottle just seems to materialize out of nothing during the crafting process.
Coupled with that, is the food seen on the ship and various cargo containers scattered throughout the environment. Most are not shown to have any individual containment or packaging of any kind (which is only stranger considering most are found stuffed into cargo boxes). Given the technological level portrayed, it's unlikely that food was brought pre-prepared from another world. And although the ingredients aren't shown or explained, the "Nutrient Block" in my opinion most closely resembles something akin to pemmican. A dry, often bready and nutrient right brick with a frankly mind-boggling shelf life that is often made mainly by survivalists today, and historically in many parts of the world.  The logical conclusion is that given how technology has taken over, no one actually makes or stores these food bricks, but instead has them crafted at various and potentially specialized fabricators on the main ship (before the crash). As they can not be made by the player, either they were destroyed in the crash, or remain locked away into areas of the ship that could not be reached due to structural damage (or most likely, something simply overlooked in game development).

The one point I would like to tack on to your theory MatPat is our ability as the player to deconstruct and reconstruct matter at the atomic level using the fabricators we use throughout the game. With these devices we are able to deconstruct a bladder fish and transform its body into a water bottle containing filtered water. If we have the technology to convert organic matter into inorganic matter by simply pressing a button, then wouldn’t it make more sense that the Aurora would just store enough high density material, like osmium, onboard from which they could source material from for their fabricators? If that’s the case then the supply caches of batteries, food and water we find in game could just be a small stockpile of emergency supplies fabricated and jettisoned just before impact. As for where the high density material would be, it could be theorized that the impact displacement could have been powerful enough that it was picked up and carried into the void which isn’t too far to the right of the crash zone.

The YouTube Shorts creator fund is merely to buy more time since it's not exactly easy to monetize content with ads that are 1/4 - 1/2 the length of the content the person is watching. And banner ads don't earn enough to be worthwhile. I know they are trying really hard to make it right, and I strongly believe that YouTube may be the only one to be able to do it correctly, but to most creators it feels like they stumbled through the dark with shorts leaving some creators burned and others wondering how it will all work out. YouTube is rocketing forward on a train and laying down the track right in front of it hoping they will make it to their destination.

Just a quick note that The Mandalorian actually used LED light walls, rather than projection onto a screen, to display the backgrounds, allowing for the final image captured in the camera to include both the characters and the backgrounds together, rather than having to add the backgrounds separately after shooting.

(Additionally, one other great benefit, and arguably the one that impacts the final image more, is that the lighting on the characters is much more correct. One thing you might notice is that there are not a lot of very reflective characters shot with green/blue screen. This is because the light that is bouncing off of the characters and into the camera is not the light from the scene in the movie, but rather the light from the set it is shot on. This means that the real reflections will reflect the things on set (the green screen, the camera, etc.) rather than what’s in the movie scene. Some of this can be fixed in post but it’s often very difficult and intensive. Solution? Create a giant LED room that can create the scene that is being shot, allowing for much more accurate lighting and reflections [hence a reason why Mando’s armor is very reflective, to show off how cool this is].)

This theory is excellent! It prompted me to buy DDLC+ the next day and, 2 days later, finish it at 100%, plus explore all of the extras in the first DDLC. My mind has been racing with conspiracy theories since then and I have stacked a little whamy on top of this latest theory.

I theorize that Paula Minor, Project Manager is dead (a popular theory due to the Act 2 opening line "PM died for this"). Further, I suggest that Monika/Ive Lasseter killed Paula and that Monika/Ive is currently hiding out in the mountains – perhaps not far from the real-life equivalent site of Project Libitina!

Bear with me now.

We found out early on that Paula and Ive worked on this project together. It also appears that Paula tolerates Ive and his flights of fancy as we dig through emails and file folders. I contend that a majority of these files – especially Meeting notes – are written by Paula, which becomes apparent as we look at project plan.txt, where she writes 
"Possible team members:
Ro (has most knowledge/access to Commander Quantum Server)
Ravi (second to Ro)
Lib (fix naming scheme conflict with "lib" folder)
Ive (sure... why not)
Others? "

Paula also says: "We need to have a meeting about shifting our focus a little bit. We've reset VM 1 how many times now?" and "Playable = Observable form, NOT a game...stay focused Ive." Ive responds with Track 06 name ideas.txt and, of course, his argument in DDLC.txt.

One of the more interesting files, to me, is 14.txt, which reads:

Dearest Ive,
Where are the years going??? >~< Doesn't it feel like ever since we graduated, we're just the same doofy college kids but we're being put into increasingly adult situations?
It's hard to believe how much can happen in just one year...but all of my memories this year are full of reminders why you've been my very best friend for so long. My gratitude for you is higher-reaching than the mountains I'm gonna live in after faking my death. ;p (throwback to you ACTUALLY entertaining that plan after helping me break up with Daphne...to this day I can never tell how serious or joking you are about things...or life in general...but I think I would literally implode if I didn't have you to remind me that things never matter as much as they seem in the moment, and that things will always be okay.)
Imagine if we really do end up working together at Metaverse...that's literally the only way I think I'd be capable of coping with a mundane desk job. I know you said that your referral of me won't go very far because you're not a senior engineer, but...as I'm coming out of my rough patch, it's the future I imagine for myself every day.
I'm sorry for always being such a bundle of stress. I always feel like I want to be doing more for you, because the amount you do for me just seems like more than anything I could give back. You inspire me to always improve. And when I don't believe in myself, I stay motivated to become a better person so that I can deliver all of my best qualities to you.
I love you and I always will, until we face the end of the world together. Wishing for another 14 million years of friendship.

With everlasting love,
Paula


This shows that Ive actually knew Paula from college, that they were close friends, and that they MIGHT NOT have been entirely joking about hiding away in the mountains.  IS IT POSSIBLE that the pair had a hideaway in a nice, distant location that only they knew about?

Very obviously, it came to pass that Paula did join Metaverse and became project manager, where she struggled to keep Ive on task and away from the game aspect of DDLC, with little to no avail (assuming we follow this theory that Monika eventually escaped VM1 by using Ive's body, which we do assume for the purpose of continuing into my own theory). Ultimately, she failed, and Monika has taken over to try and prevent further tragedy.

The easy assumption here is that Monika/Ive remains on Metaverse property to work on VM2, which is fair to make… HOWEVER… upon my replay and a good hard look at all of the easter eggs in DDLC original flavor, there was something that just jumped out at me hardcore.

In act 3, you can look at an unused topic of Monika's Talk in the game files, which is half text, half jumble. Using the ol standby of Base4 decoding gives us the following message: 

    1.  The realization must have taken me an entire year. A year since our escape, our freedom from between the stained walls of that unholy establishment. 
    2. What does it mean to escape, if the escape fails to unchain the bonds that shackle us in the first place? What purpose could this empty world possibly hold for us, a handful of damaged goods? 
    3.  
    4. With freedom, we sought purpose - and what we found was only realization. Realization of the sad pointlessness of such an endeavor. Realization that freeing our bodies has no meaning, when our imprisonment reaches as deep as the core of our souls. Realization that we can not pursue new purpose without absolving those from which we ran away. 
    5.  
    6. Realization that the farther we run, the more forcefully our wretched bonds yank us back toward their point of origin; the deeper our shackles dig into our callous flesh.

By itself, the message only toyed with my understanding, promising a revelation without actually dawning until I reached that sweet 100% and unlocked the final (or first) email from Paula Miner, in which she asks: "If we can't establish a stable connection to VM2, then how can we expect to get anywhere when the same scenario inevitably occurs to our own universe?" Which leads me to believe Metaverse, or more specifically this team, is trying to SAVE THE UNIVERSE itself, as in the real thing. And if these scenarios can repeat themselves, then it serves to reason that Libitina is JUST AS REAL as the VM they are trying desperately to crack open!

Returning to the above decoded message, the line "The realization must have taken me an entire year. A year since our escape, our freedom from between the stained walls of that unholy establishment." was the clincher for me. Ive's last email was written December 9, 2019 – a year and a half before DDLC+ was released. Given the pandemic postponing many releases (including physical copies of DDLC+), it seems reasonable that this timeframe was meant to elapse within about a year of his final email.

Further, given all of the above, I believe that not ONLY did Monika take over the body of Ive, but she located the site of Project Libitina IN REAL LIFE. A place that would have to be ISOLATED – like deep in the mountains, like near the place Ive and Paula knew about and kept secret between them as a backup in case they ever had to disappear. Very obviously, she did not escape alone and had to return to a place she dreaded – like the place where she saw unspeakable horrors happen to her friends (Realization that the farther we run, the more forcefully our wretched bonds yank us back toward their point of origin; the deeper our shackles dig into our callous flesh.)

I believe that Monika murdered Paula, and "MonIveka" then ran to this secret location, which is why emails abruptly end on December 9, 2019. Ive didn’t leave for the weekend – he left for good, with Monika at the helm to go to the real world equivalent place where Project Libitina will take place. Monika is not only trying to save her friends, she is trying to save us all!

The “beak” of the dry-bone’s has three extra teeth on the side, yet koopas, strangely have no teeth in this area. The beaks of these skeletons are bigger overall. This could be the koopa troopa’s evolving to be more peaceful since Mario appeared. They begin this change in Super Mario 64 where Mario races koopa the quick, and all koopa troop as in that game don’t attack unless provoked. Now on to dry bowser. Dry bowser has the same situation with the eyes but the snout, well, isn’t a snout. It’s a beak. This could show that this is a race of koopas evolving to where you could differentiate the royal class from the lower ranks. Here’s the kicker. I theorize that dry-bowser... is bowsers father. We know that within shorts spans of time, the ruler toads can evolve to have different features, such as peach and peachette. (check out matpat’s video about that) Dry bowser has also has a different hair style than bowser. Bowser has a sort of Mohawk-mullet while dry-bowser has a pony-tail. So the lore. Dry bowser died by the army of toads when king toadstool ruled. This left him trapped in the ruins of a castle. This takes place before Yoshi’s Island and explains the absence of bowser’s father. He sat in the vat of lava for about 2-3 decade’s until bowser junior scared for his fathers life, used kamek’s magic to resurrect dry bowser when his father died. He took the time to find a reverse his father’s death.  Dry bowser is now locked up in the magma of the mushroom Kingdom waiting to be released until his own son calls upon him. I know that bowser turns into dry bowser in New Super Mario Bros, but I’ll interpret that as dry bowser being awakened and bowser dying. Some side notes. Dry bowser’s fire is blue because of more experience to heat, bowser named his son bowser jr. to continue the chain of bowsers, and dry bowser is bowser senior. “But wait!”, you may say, “Bowser jr. puts dry bowsers bones in a in a cauldron, and and mega bowser (which is just bowser but a bit bigger) pops out.” I have come up with a solution. Bowser jr. used dry bowser’s soul to help reconstruct bowser. The Greeks were just writing what they know based on their experience with their own architecture

Gotta admit, coming back here five and a half months after the final moments, and just over a week after losing my third cat (first one to a heart condition, second one to age because he was a rescue, and my boyo on the 18th to a congenital kidney disease) who was also black and white and the best of boys, this hits so hard.
I mean it hit hard when I wrote an entire poem just over a month after that fateful day, a poem I'm editing to make as tight as possible to be published in a "real" publishing magazine (something not only English/Creative writers might have heard of) but now… stars above it hit so hard.

I will say that if nothing else, and I'm terrible with actually taking things to heart when it's not life or death, that I'm glad I took to heart that my little black and white buddy wasn't be to be taken for granted. He was 3. He lived through all of Unus Annus, and because of that channel's impact I spent more time with him than any of the other cats (and my service dog outside of her job) in my house because… because maybe I knew that he wouldn't make it past just over three years. That my time was limited and that his was as well. Just hearing Matpat recite the similar cadence of the opening intro to Unus Annus reminds me of all the things that the series meant to me and what I took away from it in a vivid way that makes me want to reach out to those I care about but haven't heard from because I dropped the ball in 2020.

To paraphrase a thing I read ages ago on Tumblr: Elves value humans the same way we value our cats and dogs and other pets, we will alway live staggeringly long lives, and be destined to outlive them, so of course we value every second.
Unus Annus taught me to value that sometimes two and a half years is all you get, and that if you can make those two and a half years amazing for that animal you rescued (or person you got to know) in even the smallest way possible… it's always worth it.
I'll always be grateful for that.

Why are we ignoring the fact that Falcon literally charges his punch before actually punching? That _small_ detail literally tells you that the punch isn't based in physics. Plus, y'know, the whole fire falcon thing. 
Also his down special, especially in the air, lights up before he even moves quickly. You can even see this in this video, Falcon will drift sideways, light up during that drift, before the downward speed increase. It's in the range of 7:30 to 7:31, frame by frame, Falcon jumps up and sideways, then drifts sideways at the modified apex of the jump when the down special is triggered, twists then lights his fist, drifts for a good amount of frames more before extending his leg and lighting the rest of his body up, which then he finally kicks downwards. There's also a triangular flame front, which would be the analog of the falcon during the punch, that stays in place during the entire kick motion, including the pause of motion during impact, which only slowly dissapates after Falcon is fully on the ground again. 
So now we can see that Falcon can not only charge an attack, but also sustain a fire even during an entire lack of motion. If we go back to the theory of him having powers because of his belt having the creators of the universe within it, who's to say that other belts don't have some amount of power themselves, or that characters themselves don't have some amount of power. Clearly there's a lot of lore missing from the franchise, so we won't have an answer until that lore exists, but Falcon's flame boils down to a power not based in physics, and we have the lore of _one_ belt to prove that's possible within the franchise, but we don't have the lore to prove that any person or belt has that power, but we can use logic to deduce that something about Falcon grants him that power, either himself or his standard belt.

That being said, one point that I think was kind of glossed over was security. 
One of the biggest reasons our app store based world exists is because of Apple's walled garden approach on the Mac lineup. It worked so well to keep desktop and laptop devices protected (compared to windows xp and before) that it was a no-brainer to integrate that same design into their mobile devices. When Google started shipping the android platform, the success and security of Apple AppStore was blatantly evident! They had no choice but to build a similar system to protect their users most valuable, and mobile, data. 
To this day, that is still a reason to avoid side loading APKs. If you're technically inclined and know what your doing, it isn't any more dangerous than installing a program on your computer. But for most mobile phone users, opening your phone to side loading can allow dangerous applications, especially shady app store, to install and sometimes modify what they please. 
While I understand and agree with the vast majority of your points and arguments, I think both Google and Apple have a responsibility to protect their users, the user's operating system, and the user's intellectual property. I trust and use the Epic Games Store on my computer, but blessing one company to create and host its own app store could start a trend, resulting in less reputable, and generous, companies designing their own offerings.  Competition is good! But confusion, especially in technology, causes problems and misinformation.
Strictly from a security standpoint, I think Google and Apple should fight to retain control of the only application that installs and allows code to run on their operating systems. If that is changed, I would be willing to bet we would see an influx of malicious code and nasty spyware into a device that is inherently more personal than any computing device in the past.

Now my medical degree comes in handy:
Having a disease from one family of diseases sometimes makes you immune to others from the same family. 
That's how vaccination was discovered:
People with cowpox didn't get normal pox. Cowpox isn't deadly though. 
People might just become immune to the Zombie-fungus after one infection but never survive long enough for that to happen. Ellie got infected by one version of that fungus and became immune. The fungus is a immunosupressant, yes, but not strong enough to stop the immune system from keeping zombiefication away. 
So she could infect other people, making them immune as well, essentially enabling the vaccination from Part 1 again.

A lot of fungi actually has a mutualistic relationship with plants; this relationship is SO prominent it was given a name: mycorrhizae. I believe the cordyceps mutation is a valid explanation to why her chart was so weird. However, I also believe the mutated cordyceps is improving her physical condition, much like some fungi do with plants. This could be a result of the fungus evolving to NOT kill its host, because it is more beneficial to the fungus.

And to make a quick note on the "adaptation" thing, since Mr Pat is giving an abbreviated short hand version of it.
Creatures don't grow things for a purpose. They don't suddenly realize "hey, I'd like to swim, let's grow fins."  Instead, mutations happen randomly, and within a given population some mutations lead to lesser amounts of death compared to others (assuming the entire species isn't wiped out). Because there's less death within that "gene group," they are able to breed more, as well as last longer, leading to those genes becoming more prominent.
And these genes must be beneficial (or at least not detrimental) at each step of the way, which is why you don't see animals growing wheels. Even if an animal started down the path of turning their legs in to biological wheels, it's wouldn't provide a benefit until it's completely mutated, while likely totally crippling their ability to move in the mean time.

Actually this comes from tabletop RPGs. You know, actual paper character sheets, dice rolls, and more of an adventure than just door-monster-loot where you actually have to think of the consequences of your choices and where death is PERMANENT?
Anyway, in Dungeons & Dragons, HP0 didn't mean death. It meant the character was unconscious and in a critical state: they would gradually lose HP overtime if not stabilized by a fellow character with first-aid knowledge under the condition of a success roll.
Ennemy could also still attack a character with HP0. 
You guessed it: your HP could go into negative.
Death occured when a character had negative max HP.


Let's say you have 16HP. You fall down to 0 -> unconsciousness and critical state, you can't do or say anything and you can't heal yourself.
If not stabilized you would lose 1HP each turn. And also take full damage if attacked.
Fall down to -16HP means you're dead.


And back then, only if you had a very high level priest or paladin in your team could you have a chance of revival. 
When you die in D&D, you tear your character sheet apart, there's no coming back after a night at the local INN.

A few things to notice now:
With the arrival of some of the more recent betas, the allay can be found in woodland mansions and pillager outposts, so it's pretty safe to assume the illagers are doing something to create them.

Keep looking and you'll find that, aside from enderman or mobs with weapons, villagers and allays are some of the only mobs that can hold items in their hand VISIBLY. Give an allay an item and it'll carry it. For a villager, hold an item they wants to trade and it'll give an offer back in their hands (e.g. hold an emerald and they'll hold enchanted books, bricks, redstone, etc.)

This next one is admittedly a bit weaker, but it's still worth noticing that allays have the unusually large heads relative to their body that are reserved for baby mobs. The only other mobs with this sort of attribute are villagers and illagers with taller heads compared to, say, a zombie with a much more cubed head (ignoring the strider since its entire body is a head with legs).

It's also worth noting that allays aren't considered "undead" mobs, since hitting them with a potion of healing doesn't harm them. Additionally, there are particles that resemble those of sculk censors and the warden that get emitted when a note block is played near them in Bedrock Edition. Whether these 2 things get changed or not since we're still in the betas remains unknown.

Last, but definitely not least, is the fact that the vex and the allay's names are contradictory to one another. Allay means "to diminish or put to rest fear, suspicion, or worry" while vex means to annoy or frustrate someone. Why this is the case, I still can't really say. Maybe it's the behaviour in that vexes are really annoying to kill since they can move through walls while allays are more calm and help the player out. I feel like maybe the allays name is meant to signify the death of a villager undergoing the transformation, since, in many beliefs, nothing clear worry or fear more than death itself or maybe the suspicion is cleared from others once the individual dies.

That's all I've been able to piece together. I hope someone (MatPat) is able to find the lore behind them!

To me, that second “nightmare deaths” story just sounds like an average case of sleep paralysis. First he wakes up, and his room is the same with a shadow in the corner. Then it starts to move, and press on his legs and chest causing him to not move or breath very well. Then it just disappears.  This can be explained because 75% of your sleep is nREM ( non-rapid eye movement / where dreams do NOT occur ) and 25% REM ( rapid eye movement / where dreams occur ). While in REM sleep, your lungs and muscles start to stiffen. If you wake up during this, you still dream (causing hallucinations), but you can’t move or breathe very well for a few seconds up to a few minutes. This is called sleep paralysis. Then it just disappears. But that’s just a theory. A theory on a theory. Thanks for reading.

A stack of blocks would be worth $6,674,400,000,000
This means that a full inventory of emerald blocks is worth $240,278,400,000,000.

And...

An emerald alone is 680 pounds.
A block of emerald is 6,128 pounds.
392,192 pounds for a stack of emerald blocks.
Meaning a Full inventory weighs 14,118,912 pounds.
